title: Al-Hadid, opening
hook: He is the First and the Last, and with you wherever you are (57:1–6)
tomorrow: what would a mountain do if the Qur'an came down on it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-Waqi'ah: the foremost, a race toward nearness that can start with a glass of water. Today, the nearness itself, and how far it travels.

Moving boxes. A packing list. A last dinner where everyone's cheerful on purpose. Leaving home comes with a question that isn't on any checklist: what comes with you, and what stays behind? The opening of al-Hadid answers in a line Pickthall renders: "and He is with you wheresoever ye may be." Not where you were raised. Not only in the masjid down the street. Wheresoever.
screen: `MOVING BOXES.` → `WHAT COMES WITH YOU?` → `WHERESOEVER YE MAY BE.`

segments.voice: Al-Hadid opens wide. Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies God; His is the sovereignty; He gives life and death. Then a line of four names in two pairs: He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and He knows all things. A bedtime prayer of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Sahih Muslim, unpacks them: the First, with nothing before; the Last, with nothing after; the Outward, with nothing above; the Inward, with nothing beneath. Then the verse that carries today. God made the heavens and the earth and established Himself on the Throne. He knows what goes down into the earth and what comes up out of it, what comes down from the sky and what rises into it. Seeds and rain, roots and prayers. "And He is with you wheresoever ye may be." Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight: one verse holds both the Throne and with you. The highest and the nearest, in a single breath, and the surah doesn't pick one. Then it closes the opening with night sliding into day, day into night, and a God who knows what's inside people's chests. For a week of leaving, this is what the tradition hands over. The One who was there first is the one who will be there last, and in between, at every new address, the same line holds. Leaving home changes your zip code. It doesn't change that.
screen: `FIRST AND LAST, OUTWARD AND INWARD.` · `WHAT GOES DOWN, WHAT RISES.` · `THE THRONE AND 'WITH YOU', ONE VERSE.` · `A NEW ADDRESS, THE SAME LINE.` · then, large: `WITH YOU.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and picture the places you'll be in the coming months: a room, a road, somewhere new. Let the line rest on each one in turn: with you, wheresoever you may be. Then picture someone you'll be apart from, and let the line rest on them as well.
Al-Hadid. Iron: surah 57, whose opening names God the First and the Last, and with you wherever you are.
Hold onto this: with you, the highest and the nearest in one verse. That one packs light.
